story: Ikara-Flinders Ranges is a park of ancient and rugged mountain landscapes, peaceful tree-lined gorges and a seasonal wealth of wildlife, with a sense of space unique to the semi-arid zone. At its centre the mountains curve into Ikara Wilpena Pound, a vast amphitheatre whose rim rises to St Mary Peak, 1,171 metres above sea level. To the north the Heysen Range runs beside the Brachina and Bunyeroo gorges, and in the Trezona formation walkers can find traces of some of the earliest life forms on earth.

The park sits in the semi-arid zone, and its life follows the rain. Spring brings a carnival of wildflowers to the plains and foothills. The yellow-footed rock-wallaby, once rare, can be seen again in Brachina and Wilkawillina gorges thanks to the Bounceback ecological restoration program, which has driven down pest animals across the Flinders and Olary bioregion; possums and quolls have also been returned to the park. Native pine groves shade the hilltops of the ABC Range, and the floor of the Pound holds mallee, native pine and heath, good country for wrens, robins, parrots and raptors.

The Adnyamathanha, whose name means hills or rock people, are the Traditional Owners, and their connection with this land stretches back many thousands of years. Ochre and charcoal paintings at Arkaroo Rock tell the creation story of Wilpena Pound; St Mary Peak is central to that story, and the Adnyamathanha would prefer that visitors do not climb to its summit. Ancient engravings of animal tracks, people and waterholes survive at Yura Mulka (Sacred Canyon), among the oldest rock engravings in the world, and at the Perawurtina Cultural Heritage Site.

Europeans brought sheep. Wilpena Station was established in 1851 and worked for 135 years; its buildings are now one of South Australia's best-preserved pastoral settlement sites. Bullock teams and coaches carrying copper, mail and produce once used Bunyeroo Gorge to reach the western plains. The park was first reserved in 1945 and now carries the Adnyamathanha name Ikara for Wilpena Pound. In 2017 Sacred Canyon was added at the request of the Adnyamathanha members of the park's co-management board.
howItWorks: Ikara-Flinders Ranges is run by the Department for Environment and Water, branded National Parks and Wildlife Service South Australia, in partnership with the Adnyamathanha people: a co-management board of Adnyamathanha and Department representatives shares responsibility and decision-making for the park's strategic management. Visitors are asked to respect cultural sites and restrictions, such as not climbing St Mary Peak's summit. Yura Mulka (Sacred Canyon) can be visited only on an Adnyamathanha guided tour, booked through Wilpena Pound Resort or another licensed operator.

South Australia charges for park entry here. Vehicle entry, priced per vehicle, must be paid online before you enter, and campsites are paid per night in advance; a 12-month pass for this park alone, or a 2- or 12-month pass covering several South Australian parks, suits regular visitors, but passes do not include camping. The park has ten National Parks campgrounds, among them Aroona, Brachina East, Trezona and the walk-in Wilcolo, booked through the parks booking system. Powered sites and permanent tents at the Wilpena Pound camp ground are run privately by Wilpena Pound Resort.

Fire rules change with the season and the day. Gas and liquid-fuel fires are allowed all year except on total fire ban days; wood fires are banned from 15 October 2026 to 24 March 2027, and firewood may never be collected in the park. On days of catastrophic fire danger the park and all walking trails close, and on extreme fire danger days the park may close. Some hikes, including St Mary Peak, Malloga Falls and Mount Ohlssen Bagge, close in December, January and February. Dogs are not permitted, except assistance dogs.

sightNotes.poi-au-ikara-flinders-ranges-ikara-wilpe: The great amphitheatre of mountains at the park's heart. Walk in to Hills Homestead and Wangara Lookout for views across the Pound floor; the Bridle Gap Hike crosses it on the Heysen Trail.
sightNotes.poi-au-ikara-flinders-ranges-st-mary-pea: At 1,171 metres the high point of the Pound rim and central to the Adnyamathanha creation story. Hike to Tanderra Saddle; the Adnyamathanha ask that you do not climb to the summit. Closed December to February.
sightNotes.poi-au-ikara-flinders-ranges-arkaroo-roc: Adnyamathanha ochre and charcoal paintings of the creation story of Wilpena Pound, on a three-kilometre return hike 17 kilometres south of Wilpena. Best in morning light.
sightNotes.poi-au-ikara-flinders-ranges-brachina-go: A gorge road through the Heysen Range, and the place to see yellow-footed rock-wallabies, at Scree Slope in the late afternoon.
sightNotes.poi-au-ikara-flinders-ranges-bunyeroo-go: A peaceful, gum-lined gorge between rugged rock formations, once a route for bullock teams and coaches; a 7.5-kilometre return hike from the Bunyeroo car park.
sightNotes.poi-au-ikara-flinders-ranges-old-wilpena: A pastoral run established in 1851 and worked for 135 years, now a well-preserved historic precinct with the self-guided Living with Land walk. Open 8 am to 5 pm.

From Leigh Creek in the north via Parachilna, entering from the north or west

planYourVisit.reservations: Pay vehicle entry online before you arrive, and book campsites in advance through the parks booking system. Book powered sites, permanent tents and Sacred Canyon tours with Wilpena Pound Resort. In November 2026 the department warned of a cyber security incident affecting Bookeasy, a third-party booking platform; check its updates before you book.

chronology.text: Adnyamathanha ancestors paint Arkaroo Rock and engrave the walls of Yura Mulka (Sacred Canyon).
Wilpena Station is established as a pastoral run; it works for 135 years.
The photographer Harold Cazneaux camps and photographs in the area in May, a journey now followed by the Spirit of Endurance Trail.
Sacred Canyon is added to the park at the request of Adnyamathanha board members.
From 1 April, Sacred Canyon is open only on Adnyamathanha guided tours, and Wilcolo campground replaces Cooinda inside the Pound.

safety: Summer temperatures reach 30 to 45°C. Walk in the cool of the day, start the St Mary Peak hike by 9 am (10 am in daylight saving), and carry at least four litres of water per person on walks over two hours.
Carry maps, a compass, a whistle and a jacket, register at the Wilpena trailhead for walks of three hours or more, and tell someone your route: searches start only when walkers are reported overdue.
Mobile coverage is patchy, especially in low-lying areas. In an emergency call 000; the NPWS SA after-hours duty officer is on 0408 378 284.
Unsealed roads change with the weather. Drive slowly and check the Outback Road Report.
Rock climbing and abseiling are at your own risk, only in the designated zone.
regulations: Pay vehicle entry and campsite fees before you enter the park.
Visit Yura Mulka (Sacred Canyon) only with an Adnyamathanha guide; please do not climb to the summit of St Mary Peak.
No wood fires from 15 October 2026 to 24 March 2027, no fires of any kind on total fire ban days, and no firewood collection at any time.
No dogs, except assistance dogs on a lead.
Do not touch or remove anything at cultural sites, and take all your rubbish with you.

weather: The Flinders Ranges have a semi-arid climate. Mild temperatures from April to October make that the most comfortable time for bushwalking and cycling, and spring brings the wildflowers. Summer is hot, with maximums of 30 to 45°C, high fire danger and summer closures of the longer hikes. Water is not guaranteed anywhere in the park: carry at least four litres per person for walks of more than two hours. Unsealed roads can be affected by rain, so check the Outback Road Report.
directions: The park is about 450 kilometres north of Adelaide in the central Flinders Ranges. From Adelaide, take one of several routes to Hawker, then follow the signs to Wilpena. From Leigh Creek, head south to Parachilna and enter from the north or west, or go east towards Vulkathunha-Gammon Ranges National Park and follow the signs south. From Broken Hill, turn north at Yunta on the Arkaroola Road towards Blinman. The main road into Wilpena Pound is sealed; the other roads are unsealed but open to high-clearance two-wheel-drive vehicles, caravans and trailers. Check the Outback Road Report (1300 361 033) before you go.
